segments.narration: Why does future you feel like a stranger your brain is willing to betray?
segments.screenAction: Split screen showing present self enjoying distractions while future self looks increasingly stressed and overwhelmed
segments.expectedResult: Viewers recognize their own procrastination patterns and feel intrigued
segments.visualPurpose: Immediately establishes the core conflict between present and future self

segments.narration: Your brain's temporal discounting system makes immediate rewards feel more valuable than future ones.
segments.screenAction: Animation showing brain regions lighting up when presented with immediate vs delayed rewards
segments.expectedResult: Viewers understand the biological basis of procrastination
segments.visualPurpose: Visualizes the neuroscience concept in an accessible way

segments.narration: This isn't laziness—it's your brain's survival mechanism prioritizing the present.
segments.screenAction: Historical timeline showing how temporal discounting evolved in humans for survival
segments.expectedResult: Viewers reframe procrastination as a biological trait, not a character flaw
segments.visualPurpose: Provides evolutionary context to reduce self-blame

segments.narration: When we procrastinate, we're essentially mugging our future selves.
segments.screenAction: Metaphorical animation showing present self stealing resources from future self
segments.expectedResult: Viewers feel the consequences of their procrastination more personally
segments.visualPurpose: Makes abstract consequences tangible and relatable

segments.narration: The key is making your future self feel more present and real to your brain.
segments.screenAction: Interactive exercise where viewers visualize their future self in detail
segments.expectedResult: Viewers begin to develop empathy for their future selves
segments.visualPurpose: Engages viewers in a practical exercise to bridge the temporal gap

segments.narration: Implementation intentions: if-then planning bridges the present-future divide.
segments.screenAction: Before-and-after examples showing how specific if-then statements reduce procrastination
segments.expectedResult: Viewers learn a concrete technique to apply immediately
segments.visualPurpose: Demonstrates the solution with clear, actionable examples

segments.narration: Rewire your relationship with time by making your future self feel like someone worth helping today.
segments.screenAction: Present and future selves reaching across time to high-five, merging into one
segments.expectedResult: Viewers feel empowered to change their relationship with time
segments.visualPurpose: Provides a hopeful, actionable closing image
